ledger.hypothesis: This node is ELEMENTWISE, not query-shaped: one sin per vertex over a 159,602-vert polySphere. The arithmetic cannot be the bottleneck, so the cost has to be per-access overhead and whole-array temporaries -- the lowered nd form materialised six of them (a push_back'd std::vector<double>, a from_data copy, a .copy(), two column slices and the sin result) and then paid two more 5 MB gather/scatter copies with a float<->double conversion per element in allPositions/setAllPositions. Removing levels of copying, not making the sin cheaper, is the lever.
ledger.risk: Writing through a const_cast'd getRawPoints() bypasses MItGeometry, so it is only valid when the deformer set covers every vertex (guarded by nv == iter.count(), with the original MItGeometry path kept as the fallback) and only if the output mesh is a genuine private copy rather than a COW alias of the input -- an alias would silently deform an already-deformed mesh. Also float storage: the kernel widens float->double, does the identical double arithmetic, and stores back through the same single round-to-nearest that setAllPositions would have applied, so it is bit-identical rather than a precision shortcut.
ledger.theme: Fuse the nd expression tree into one loop, then stop round-tripping 160k verts through an MPointArray at all -- deform the output mesh's own float point buffer in place, with a persistent per-node pool mapping over disjoint vertex ranges.
